title: Parallel Computing & Performance (CPU to GPU)
tagline: Make code fast by making it parallel.
summary: Make code fast by making it parallel. You start with the laws of parallelism (Amdahl, Gustafson, scalability) and CPU parallelism done right — thread pools, the C++17 parallel STL, and load balancing — then go deep on data parallelism with SIMD/AVX, and finally cross to the GPU: CUDA fundamentals (the SIMT model, threads/blocks/warps, the memory hierarchy), and GPU performance engineering (memory coalescing, shared-memory tiling, occupancy, reductions). The track culminates in optimizing a real compute kernel — matrix multiply — from a naive loop all the way to a tiled CUDA kernel, measured against hardware peak and vendor libraries. This is the performance-and-parallelism track of the Zero-to-Low-Level-Systems-Elite program and the direct on-ramp to the AI-chip / ML-systems branch, where GPUs run the math behind modern AI.

capstone.title: GEMM Optimization Lab — From Naive Loop to Tiled CUDA Kernel
capstone.project: Optimize the workhorse of modern computing — dense matrix multiply (GEMM) — through every level of the parallel stack. Implement it naive, then cache-blocked, then multithreaded, then SIMD-vectorized on the CPU, then as a CUDA kernel, and finally a shared-memory tiled CUDA kernel. Measure GFLOP/s at each stage against the machine's theoretical peak and a vendor library (BLAS / cuBLAS), and write up where each speedup came from.

phases.title: Foundations of Parallelism
phases.goal: Reason about parallel speedup: concurrency vs parallelism, Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws, scalability and efficiency, and task vs data parallelism.

projects.title: Concurrency vs Parallelism
projects.description: Build and time programs that demonstrate the concrete difference between concurrency (interleaving on one thread) and parallelism (simultaneous execution on multiple cores), then survey the three hardware parallelism levels — multi-core, SIMD, and GPU.

projects.title: Amdahl's Law
projects.description: Implement Amdahl's Law formula, tabulate predicted speedup curves for serial fractions 1–50%, parallelize a prefix-sum workload, measure its scaling from 1–8 threads, and fit the formula to recover the program's empirical serial fraction.

projects.title: Gustafson's Law & Weak Scaling
projects.description: Implement Gustafson's Law formula alongside Amdahl's, run a weak scaling experiment where problem size grows proportionally with thread count, measure weak scaling efficiency, and decide which scaling model applies to real-world system designs.

projects.title: Speedup, Efficiency & Scalability
projects.description: Build a professional scaling study: measure parallel dot product and Mandelbrot speedup from 1 to N threads, compute parallel efficiency at each point, isolate four overhead sources with micro-benchmarks, and diagnose bottleneck type from the efficiency curve shape.

projects.title: Task vs Data Parallelism
projects.description: Implement data parallelism (image blur split across rows) and task parallelism (3-stage producer-consumer pipeline) for the same processing workload, measure their performance profiles, demonstrate Monte Carlo as an embarrassingly parallel benchmark, and build a decision framework for choosing the right decomposition.

projects.title: Decomposing a Problem
projects.description: Apply block, cyclic, and dynamic partitioning strategies to an irregular workload, measure load imbalance for each, then run a 2D domain decomposition experiment demonstrating how row-major vs column-major partition alignment affects cache performance by more than 3×.

projects.title: The Costs of Going Parallel
projects.description: Build five targeted overhead micro-experiments — thread creation, uncontended vs contended mutex, false sharing, and memory bandwidth saturation — then combine all overhead sources into a deliberately bad parallel design that is measurably slower than serial with every thread count.

projects.title: Scaling Study Lab
projects.description: Complete a professional parallel scaling study: parallelize a 2D Gaussian convolution with correct decomposition, false-sharing avoidance, and median timing; run from 1 to N threads; compute speedup and efficiency; fit Amdahl's Law to the data; and write a structured performance report with bottleneck identification in journal/.

phases.title: CPU Parallelism at Scale
phases.goal: Use all your cores well: thread pools, work distribution and load balancing, the C++17 parallel STL (std::execution), and parallel reduction patterns.

projects.title: Parallelizing a Loop with Threads
projects.description: Split a 500 M-element reduction loop across std::thread workers, combine partial results, and measure speedup vs thread count — the manual baseline before higher-level abstractions.

projects.title: Building a Thread Pool
projects.description: Implement a ThreadPool class with a mutex-protected task queue, std::packaged_task for future-returning submit(), and graceful shutdown — then benchmark it against per-task thread creation.

projects.title: Load Balancing & Work Stealing
projects.description: Contrast static vs dynamic scheduling on imbalanced tasks using an atomic counter, measure the speedup from dynamic dispatch, and study the per-thread-deque work-stealing design used by TBB and Rayon.

projects.title: The C++17 Parallel STL
projects.description: Apply std::execution::par and par_unseq to for_each, transform, reduce, and sort; measure par vs seq speedup across data sizes; understand the TBB backend requirement and floating-point non-determinism of parallel reduce.

projects.title: Parallel Reduction & Scan
projects.description: Implement tree reduction with per-thread partial sums, demonstrate why shared-atomic accumulation serializes cores, use std::reduce with its associativity caveat, and implement parallel prefix-sum scan.

projects.title: Parallel Patterns: Map, Reduce, Pipeline
projects.description: Implement and benchmark the five core parallel skeletons — map, reduce, map-reduce (word count), pipeline (bounded queue), and fork-join (recursive async) — and learn to match each pattern to the right problem.

projects.title: Concurrent Data Structures & Sharing
projects.description: Measure false sharing on parallel histogram counters, fix it with alignas(64) padding, then implement per-thread aggregation to achieve 40x speedup over shared atomics — the universal high-throughput parallel counting pattern.

projects.title: Multicore Optimization Lab
projects.description: Apply thread pool dispatch, per-thread unordered_map aggregation, and parallel-STL sort to a 64-document word-count corpus; run a full scaling study from 1 to 8 threads reporting speedup and parallel efficiency.

phases.title: SIMD & Data Parallelism
phases.goal: Do many operations per instruction: vectorization, AVX intrinsics, alignment and data layout, and writing SIMD algorithms that the compiler can't auto-generate.

projects.title: What is SIMD?
projects.description: Explore the SIMD execution model by probing CPU vector ISA support, measuring scalar vs AVX2 array-add throughput, and understanding register widths across the SSE/AVX/AVX-512 family.

projects.title: Auto-Vectorization
projects.description: Write loops the compiler can auto-vectorize, read -fopt-info-vec reports, and systematically remove vectorization blockers including aliasing, loop-carried dependencies, and non-unit stride access.

projects.title: AVX Intrinsics Basics
projects.description: Hand-write a SAXPY kernel using __m256, _mm256_loadu_ps, and _mm256_fmadd_ps, then compare its throughput against scalar and auto-vectorized versions to understand when intrinsics add value.

projects.title: Alignment & Data Layout for SIMD
projects.description: Benchmark a particle physics update in Array-of-Structs vs Struct-of-Arrays layout, measure the SIMD throughput difference, and learn to use alignas(32) and std::aligned_alloc correctly.

projects.title: SIMD Reductions & Horizontal Ops
projects.description: Implement vectorized array sum and dot product using multi-lane FMA accumulators and a hadd/extractf128 horizontal reduction, measuring throughput and examining the floating-point associativity implications.

projects.title: SIMD with Branches: Masking & Blend
projects.description: Replace per-lane conditional branches with compare-and-blendv patterns to implement threshold filtering and ReLU activation using AVX2, measuring throughput and understanding the GPU warp divergence analogy.

projects.title: Practical SIMD Algorithms
projects.description: Implement a complete RGB-to-grayscale + threshold image processing pipeline in scalar and AVX2, measure end-to-end speedup, and evaluate the portability tradeoff between raw intrinsics and cross-platform SIMD libraries.

projects.title: SIMD Optimization Lab
projects.description: Vectorize a batched L2 normalization kernel using the full SIMD toolkit — auto-vectorization, manual AVX2+FMA with 4-accumulator reduction, and OpenMP multithreading — then produce a speedup breakdown table and efficiency analysis vs theoretical peak.

phases.title: GPU Programming I — CUDA Fundamentals
phases.goal: Program the GPU: the SIMT model, threads/blocks/grids/warps, the device memory hierarchy, writing and launching your first kernels, and host/device data movement.

projects.title: The GPU & the SIMT Model
projects.description: Set up a CUDA environment and write your first device kernel, learning the CPU-vs-GPU design tradeoff, the SIMT execution model, warps, and the Streaming Multiprocessor hierarchy.

projects.title: Your First Kernel — Vector Add
projects.description: Implement GPU vector addition end-to-end: cudaMalloc, H2D copy, a __global__ kernel using the global index formula, D2H copy, verification, and a grid-stride loop for arbitrary array sizes.

projects.title: GPU Memory Management
projects.description: Benchmark and compare pageable host memory, pinned (page-locked) host memory, and Unified Memory for GPU data transfer, quantifying bandwidth differences and learning when each approach is appropriate.

projects.title: Threads, Blocks & Grids in Depth
projects.description: Map 2D problems (images, matrices) to 2D CUDA grids using dim3, apply boundary checks for non-multiple dimensions, study how block size affects occupancy, and use a 2D grid-stride loop for arbitrary-size problems.

projects.title: Errors, Synchronization & Timing
projects.description: Write a CUDA_CHECK macro for robust error handling, demonstrate why CPU-side timing is wrong for asynchronous kernels, and build a correct cudaEvent_t timing harness — the professional foundation for all future kernel benchmarking.

projects.title: Warps & Warp Divergence
projects.description: Measure the cost of intra-warp branch divergence, write branchless alternatives using CUDA math intrinsics, and restructure a reduction kernel to be warp-uniform — learning the pattern that prevents the most common GPU performance pitfall.

projects.title: 2D Kernels — Image & Matrix Processing
projects.description: Write a complete 2D box-blur image filter and a matrix transpose kernel, applying dim3 2D launches, clamped boundary handling, CUDA_CHECK error checking, and cudaEvent timing — and observe why naive transpose is bandwidth-limited by strided writes.

projects.title: CUDA Fundamentals Lab
projects.description: Build a complete GPU image processing pipeline (5x5 Gaussian blur + Sobel edge detection) integrating pinned memory, __constant__ memory, CUDA_CHECK error handling, GPU event timing, and a CPU-vs-GPU speedup comparison — the phase capstone.

phases.title: GPU Programming II — Performance
phases.goal: Make GPU kernels fast: memory coalescing, shared-memory tiling, occupancy, warp divergence, efficient reductions, and profiling with Nsight.

projects.title: Memory Coalescing
projects.description: Benchmark coalesced vs strided global memory access patterns to quantify the bandwidth penalty of uncoalesced loads and writes on a real GPU.

projects.title: Shared Memory
projects.description: Implement the staging pattern using __shared__ memory to build a latency microbenchmark and a 1D stencil kernel that reduces global memory traffic by exploiting data reuse.

projects.title: Tiled Matrix Multiply
projects.description: Implement the canonical tiled GEMM kernel using shared memory to reduce global memory traffic by a factor of TILE and measure the resulting GFLOP/s speedup over the naive kernel.

projects.title: Shared Memory Bank Conflicts
projects.description: Measure the performance penalty of 32-way shared memory bank conflicts in a matrix transpose, then eliminate them with +1 padding and verify the speedup and bank assignment analytically.

projects.title: Occupancy & Launch Configuration
projects.description: Measure how block size, register count, and shared memory allocation affect SM occupancy, then observe the relationship between occupancy and throughput for both memory-bound and compute-bound kernels.

projects.title: Efficient Parallel Reductions
projects.description: Implement the 5-step reduction optimization progression — from naive interleaved to warp-shuffle __shfl_down_sync — measuring the effective bandwidth at each step and explaining each bottleneck fixed.

projects.title: Profiling with Nsight
projects.description: Use Nsight Compute to profile naive and tiled GEMM kernels, read the key metrics (SM throughput, stall reasons, memory bandwidth %, occupancy), and follow the optimize-measure loop to connect profiler output to code fixes.

projects.title: GPU Optimization Lab
projects.description: Apply the complete Phase 5 optimization stack (coalescing, shared memory staging, bank conflict padding, occupancy tuning) to a matrix transpose kernel, measuring bandwidth and profiling with Nsight at each step from 8% to 83%+ of peak.

phases.title: HPC, Heterogeneous Computing & the Capstone
phases.goal: Tie it together: OpenMP and NUMA-aware scaling, the CPU-vs-GPU tradeoff, and a capstone optimizing matrix multiply from naive to tiled CUDA against hardware peak.

projects.title: OpenMP: Parallelism with Pragmas
projects.description: Parallelize loops with #pragma omp parallel for, write correct parallel reductions, compare scheduling strategies, and benchmark OpenMP against parallel STL on a shared-memory machine.

projects.title: OpenMP Advanced: Tasks, Collapse, and False Sharing
projects.description: Use OpenMP tasks for recursive parallelism, collapse(2) for nested loops, atomic/critical/reduction for shared state, and diagnose and fix false sharing between OpenMP threads.

projects.title: NUMA & Memory Affinity
projects.description: Measure local vs remote NUMA memory access bandwidth, fix NUMA-unaware allocation using first-touch initialization, and control thread/memory placement with numactl and OMP_PROC_BIND.

projects.title: Choosing CPU vs GPU: The Throughput/Latency/Transfer Tradeoff
projects.description: Measure PCIe transfer bandwidth, find the CPU vs GPU break-even problem size for elementwise ops, apply the roofline model to classify operations as bandwidth or compute bound, and build a decision framework.

projects.title: CUDA Streams & Overlap: Hiding Transfer Latency
projects.description: Use cudaMemcpyAsync and multiple CUDA streams to overlap PCIe data transfers with GPU kernel execution, measure the speedup from 2-stream and 4-stream pipelines, and understand multi-GPU dispatch with cudaSetDevice.

projects.title: Standing on Giants: BLAS, cuBLAS, and Thrust
projects.description: Call cuBLAS sgemm to perform GEMM and compare GFLOP/s against a naive kernel and the theoretical peak; use Thrust device algorithms without writing kernels; and build a decision framework for library vs custom kernel.

projects.title: Performance Methodology End-to-End
projects.description: Apply the measure → roofline → bottleneck → fix → repeat optimization loop to a 2D convolution: use perf stat to identify cache bottlenecks, apply tiling and OpenMP, and report results honestly with GFLOP/s, % of peak, speedup, and machine context.

projects.title: GEMM Optimization Lab (Track Capstone)
projects.description: Optimize dense matrix multiply through the full stack: naive → cache-blocked → OpenMP → AVX2 → OpenBLAS on CPU, and naive CUDA → shared-memory tiled → cuBLAS on GPU. Report GFLOP/s and % of peak at every stage; package with CMake + GoogleTest; explain every speedup with roofline reasoning and document two tradeoffs.
